title: The World Cup Starts Wednesday. Five Million NRIs in North America Have Front-Row Seats.
excerpt: India is not playing, but the diaspora does not need a team on the pitch to show up. A guide to watching, attending, and making the most of the biggest World Cup ever held.
body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off on Wednesday, June 11, when Mexico face South Africa at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. Over the next five weeks, 48 teams will play 104 matches across 16 stadiums in the United States, Canada, and Mexico — making this the largest World Cup in the tournament's 96-year history.

India did not qualify. That much is familiar. But for the estimated five million Indians and Indian-Americans living in North America, this World Cup is different. It is not happening on a television at 2 AM. It is happening down the road.

## Where to Watch in India

https://x.com/FIFAWorldCup/status/2063954511849554074

After months of uncertainty, Zee Entertainment confirmed an eight-year deal with FIFA covering 39 events from 2026 through 2034. The 2026 World Cup will air live on **Unite8 Sports** — Zee's newly launched sports network — in Hindi and English across four channels: Unite8 Sports 1, Unite8 Sports 1 HD, Unite8 Sports 2, and Unite8 Sports 2 HD.

Streaming will be available on **ZEE5**. This is a shift from the 2022 cycle, when Viacom18 handled coverage through Sports18 and JioCinema. Viewers should update their ZEE5 apps and confirm their TV provider listings before the opening match.

## The NRI Advantage: Venues in Desi Strongholds

Several host cities sit in the heart of America's largest Indian communities. The World Cup final on July 19 will be played at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey — a short drive from Jackson Heights, Queens, home to one of the densest concentrations of South Asian life anywhere outside the subcontinent.

Other matches fall in equally familiar territory:

- **San Francisco Bay Area** — Qatar vs Switzerland at Levi's Stadium on June 13. Silicon Valley's enormous Indian population — Fremont, Sunnyvale, Santa Clara — is a short drive away.
- **Houston** — Matches at NRG Stadium throughout the group stage. The Hillcroft corridor is one of America's richest Indo-Pak dining and shopping districts.
- **Toronto** — Canada vs Bosnia and Herzegovina at BMO Field on June 12. Brampton and Scarborough's South Asian communities are the largest in Canada.
- **Dallas** — Semi-final venue at AT&T Stadium. The DFW Metroplex has one of the fastest-growing Indian populations in the US.
- **Los Angeles** — Multiple matches at SoFi Stadium. Artesia's Little India is a cultural landmark for the diaspora.

Even if you cannot attend a match, every major metro with an Indian community will have watch parties, pub screenings, and community gatherings. Jacksonville, for instance, has already announced screenings at multiple venues with dedicated schedules for every group stage match.

## Tickets: What to Know

The Last-Minute Sales Phase is open on FIFA.com. Prices start at approximately $120 for neutral group-stage matches and climb steeply for knockout rounds — semi-final tickets begin around $930, and final tickets start near $5,785. All prices carry a 15% FIFA service fee.

**Only buy from FIFA.com or the Official Resale Marketplace.** Tickets from unofficial resellers may not scan at the gate. All tickets are mobile-only and delivered through the FIFA World Cup 2026 app.

For NRIs travelling from India, budget roughly ₹4-6 lakh per person for a two-week trip including flights, accommodation, food, and match tickets. Staying in Indian-enclave neighbourhoods — Brampton in Toronto, Artesia in Los Angeles, Santa Clara in the Bay Area — can cut accommodation and food costs significantly.

## The Schedule: Key Dates

| Stage | Dates |
|-------|-------|
| Group stages | June 11 – 27 |
| Round of 32 | June 28 – July 3 |
| Round of 16 | July 4 – 7 |
| Quarter-finals | July 9 – 11 |
| Semi-finals | July 14 – 15 |
| Third-place playoff | July 18 |
| **Final** | **July 19** (MetLife Stadium, New York) |

The opening match is Mexico vs South Africa on June 11 at 3 PM ET. Brazil's first match — against Morocco — is on June 13 at MetLife Stadium at 6 PM ET.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

India's absence from the pitch does not diminish the diaspora's relationship with this tournament. Millions of NRIs follow the Premier League, La Liga, and Serie A with genuine passion. Many are fans of Brazil, Argentina, Germany, or England. Some will root for the four players of Indian origin who did qualify — including New Zealand's Sarpreet Singh.

And for the first time, the World Cup is structured to be experienced in person by the diaspora rather than watched from afar. The venues overlap almost perfectly with the cities where Indian-Americans have built their lives.

If you live in the Bay Area, New York, Houston, Toronto, Dallas, or Los Angeles, the biggest sporting event on earth is, for once, in your neighbourhood.

*The first ball is kicked on Wednesday. Be there.*
